C (data) says no 1327-byte Cosmic decrypt exists and SHA-256 4f7a1e… is a fabrication; issue #56 XOR-of-7 "does not reproduce its own claimed plaintext SHA". Prior report §4.5/§8 reproduced a 1,327-byte Cosmic output with exactly that SHA-256 via the raw-password/MD5 construction. C tested the XOR as EVP passphrase (raw+hex, KDF unstated = harness default SHA-256) and as a direct AES key with IV∈{0,salt}; the demo uses a different token list (…yellowblueprimes, yinyang instead of yourlastcommand, secondanswer) and raw-key/IV=salt. No C entry tests EVP-MD5 with the raw 32-byte XOR as password. Prior report is better supported (exact byte reproduction); C's negative does not cover the reproduced convention. Significance of the bytes remains unverified either way.

C asserts Salted__ ⇒ "-pass mode; raw-key / custom-IV / alternate-KDF is impossible" and that Cosmic/small blobs "use standard SHA-256 EVP" (inferred from non-hits). Prior report §3.1: Salted__ and ciphertext length specify neither cipher, digest, password representation nor iteration count; MD5-EVP links reproduce. C partly self-corrects (L3993: PBKDF2 -iter writes identical header; earlier "iteration axis closed" was an over-claim). Prior report better supported.

C states an 80-byte ciphertext decrypts to 64 bytes = "exactly two 32-byte keys". Prior report §4.1: valid PKCS#7 permits 64–79 bytes; the reproduced chains yield 79-byte outputs (32/32/15). C's statement is wrong as a general claim; its address detector (32-byte windows) partly compensates.

C reports salph_inner resisted ~33.5M decrypts and p32_trailing has "no community attack history". Prior report §10 reproduces chain 1 (UTF-8 "matrixsumlistenterlastwordsbeforearchichoicethispasswordmatrixsumlist", EVP-MD5, 79 bytes) and chain 2 on p32_trailing, first published in A PR#68 comment 2026-01-01. C contains no entry for this construction, Naddiseo#13/#14/#17 or PR#68's comment; its nearest test (soup-4 concat without trailing matrixsumlist, literal/sha forms, default SHA-256 KDF, readability gate) does not cover it. Not a contradiction of bytes, but C's novelty and exhaustion claims are contradicted.

C labels the faed Bifid "btcseed" fragment unverified/"coincidental", saying the construction is under-specified and could not be reproduced deterministically. C's Bifid demos use a 3×3 Polybius square over a–i (and identity/Lo Shu/reversed squares). Prior report §4.4 reproduced the full 570-letter output with the 5×5 square DBIFHCEGAKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ, period 570, decrypt (C's own sourceQuote says period 570). C's non-reproduction rests on a mis-modelled cipher; prior report better supported on the mechanics (intendedness still open).

Prior report §8/§11: a deterministic seed-and-counter derivation can also be filtered for a vanity prefix. Prior better supported (C's argument excludes only one-shot phrase hashing).
